title: Cartographer's Revenge
desc: Phantom islands, geopolitical absurdities & places the GPS forgot

questions.q: Null Island is at coordinates 0°N 0°E. What's actually there?
questions.a: A weather buoy in the Gulf of Guinea — the coordinates exist where the equator meets the prime meridian, in open ocean

questions.q: The Danakil Depression in Ethiopia is one of the hottest inhabited places on Earth. What's the average annual temperature?
What is an 'exclave' and which European country has one completely surrounded by Switzerland?
questions.a: An exclave is territory separated from the main body. Büsingen am Hochrhein is a German exclave entirely within Switzerland

questions.q: Sandy Island appeared on maps and Google Earth near New Caledonia for over a century. What happened when scientists went to find it in 2012?
questions.a: It didn't exist — it was a phantom island, likely from a 19th-century cartographic error

questions.q: The Dead Sea is shrinking by roughly how much per year?
questions.a: About 1 metre (3.3 feet) per year — it's lost roughly a third of its surface area since the 1960s

questions.q: Bir Tawil is a region between Egypt and Sudan that neither country claims. Why?
questions.a: Both countries claim the adjacent, larger Hala'ib Triangle instead — claiming Bir Tawil would mean giving up Hala'ib

questions.q: Which country has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
questions.a: Italy (59 as of 2024), followed closely by China

questions.q: The Mariana Trench is the deepest point in the ocean. More people have walked on the Moon than have visited the bottom — true or false?
questions.a: True — 12 people have walked on the Moon, while only a handful have reached Challenger Deep

questions.q: What is a 'tripoint' and where do three European countries meet at a single bench?
questions.a: A tripoint is where three borders meet. The Dreiländereck bench sits at the junction of Germany, France, and Switzerland near Basel

questions.q: Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa. But which country is the world's largest 'country within a country' by area?
questions.a: Trick question — Lesotho is the only country entirely enclosed by a single other country. San Marino and Vatican City are enclosed by Italy, but they're smaller
